181a15: Those [arguments] that depend on begging and assuming what is at the start
181a16: when put to the questioner, if it is evident, must not be conceded, nor even if it is reputable,
181a19: once the discussion has proceeded; for the refutation must be without [assumption of] the original point. Then, that it was conceded
181a20: not as something to be used as such, but as something to be used to reason toward this point,
181a21: is the opposite of what holds in the case of the fallacious refutations.
